no nuclear-specific transparency audit is supplied.","duplicate_reporting":"The chapter has very few distinct locators; repeated contextual indicators and reused diplomatic material must not be counted as independent claim units.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both favorable posture evidence and adverse or unresolved-risk themes were identified, but the search breadth for nuclear rhetoric, dual-use governance, command safety, and consequential-risk episodes is incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Missing primary nuclear-policy, dual-use governance, command-and-control, safety, and local-language reporting sources.","official_claim_independence":"Japanese and Indonesian official records establish statements or formal frameworks, not independent verification of efficacy or safety.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Not a major demonstrated risk for this chapter; however, absence of complaints cannot establish safety in a specialized domain.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"SIPRI and IAEA establish national exposure and longstanding baseline; ruler authority, inherited posture, and external 2022 shocks are not sufficiently linked to a specific decision.","supporting_evidence_ids":["RC001","RC002","RC003","RC004","RC005","LF077","LF152"],"unresolved_risks":["No direct ruler-attributed existential-risk decision or dual-use governance episode.","Country non-nuclear status may be mistaken for personal conduct.","Precise locator yield is insufficient for several mapped claims."]},"chapter_id":"1B","defensible_evidence_estimate":5,"independent_source_family_estimate":4,"missing_themes":["Ruler-attributed nuclear or dual-use governance decision","Command, safety, or escalation episode","Direct evidence of consequential risk reduction","Specific adverse and contrary evidence beyond national exposure"],"substantive_issues":["National exposure and safeguards are not equivalent to ruler conduct.","Further bounded research could recover attribution and precise locators."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"RC003-RC006 and RC020 document presidential or official diplomatic actions; RC007 reports contested Papua findings and separates state and non-state responsibility.","closed_system_silence":"Papua is identified as an information black spot, so official casualty and conduct accounts may omit abuses or civilian-protection failures.","duplicate_reporting":"Ukraine, Myanmar, and Papua claims appear in reused IDs; the low locator count makes underlying-fact duplication a material risk.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Favorable diplomacy and peace-effort evidence was collected alongside adverse Papua conflict and civilian-protection evidence, but searches for orders, rules of engagement, arms recipients, and accountability remain incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Missing primary military directives, civilian-protection orders, recipient/end-use records, independent Papua field reporting, and accountability-case documentation.","official_claim_independence":"RC006 and RC020 support the fact of Indonesian policy statements but do not independently establish implementation or efficacy; RC003 is an official diplomatic record with similar limits.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Complaint and conflict reporting may overrepresent accessible or media-visible incidents, while Papua restrictions may suppress volume; neither direction is quantified.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Local conflict counts and military spending establish exposure and baseline; attribution is shared or contested, and Ukraine, COVID recovery, and regional conflict shocks are not fully separated from presidential responsibility.","supporting_evidence_ids":["RC003","RC004","RC005","RC006","RC007","RC020","LF073","LF076","LS042","LS043"],"unresolved_risks":["Papua attribution and civilian-protection responsibility remain incomplete.","Diplomatic action is better evidenced than outcome or correction.","Potentially important local-language and primary security sources are absent."]},"chapter_id":"2B","defensible_evidence_estimate":7,"independent_source_family_estimate":5,"missing_themes":["Civilian-protection orders and rules of engagement","Arms recipients and end-use accountability","Independent evidence on Papua accountability and remedy","Contrary evidence on diplomatic or peace-effort effectiveness"],"substantive_issues":["Do not convert contested state/non-state conflict reporting into automatic presidential responsibility.","Another bounded search could materially improve attribution and contrary evidence."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"RC008-RC013 generally identify reports, documented restrictions, institutional actions, and legal provisions; IDs are reusable, but precise locators and claim splitting remain necessary.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse rights evidence and some favorable evidence of civil-society and media operation were both identified; searches for presidential rhetoric, remedy effectiveness, prison conditions, and vulnerable-group protection remain incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Missing primary court, prison, complaint, remedy, police/military disciplinary, and vulnerable-group/local-language documentation.","official_claim_independence":"RC008 is official external reporting and RC011-RC013 are NGO assessments; no systematic independent verification of government denials or remedy claims is supplied.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Open reporting and NGO complaint activity can increase apparent severity relative to closed systems, while Papua and surveillance can suppress reporting; prevalence cannot be inferred from report volume.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Local indicators establish national and longitudinal context; attribution varies by institution and locality, and COVID recovery, Papua conflict, and inherited legal structures are not fully disentangled.","supporting_evidence_ids":["RC007","RC008","RC009","RC010","RC011","RC012","RC013","LF322","LF331","LF440","LF445","LS003","LS011"],"unresolved_risks":["Direct presidential direction, knowledge, tolerance, correction, and remedy effectiveness are unevenly evidenced.","The Criminal Code evidence spans 2019 and 2022 and needs strict period separation.","Important vulnerable-group and prison evidence is missing."]},"chapter_id":"3B","defensible_evidence_estimate":8,"independent_source_family_estimate":6,"missing_themes":["Direct presidential rhetoric or incitement","Remedy and accountability effectiveness","Prison conditions","Vulnerable-group protection","Independent primary corroboration of key allegations"],"substantive_issues":["Country-level rights indicators cannot alone establish personal attribution.","Continuation could materially improve event-level findings and contrary evidence."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"RC011-RC013 and RC012 distinguish comparative assessments, reported pressure, legal provisions, and institutional context; only distinct source-locator-claim units should count.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"The notebook includes competitive political space and independent media as favorable context and restrictions/manipulation as adverse evidence, but primary searches for the election-delay controversy and election-institution influence are incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Missing primary election-administration records, court or parliamentary records, direct presidential statements, implementation guidance, and independent local monitoring.","official_claim_independence":"Official records establish formal acts but do not independently validate institutional independence or implementation; NGO assessments provide external checks but may share reporting ecosystems.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Open complaints and media reporting may make deterioration more visible, whereas pressure and surveillance may suppress complaints; no denominator or complaint-volume audit is supplied.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Local indicators address institutional baseline and exposure; executive, legislative, judicial, and subnational authority are not fully separated, and COVID-era conditions may affect 2022 comparisons.","supporting_evidence_ids":["RC011","RC012","RC013","LF616","LF623","LF884","LF898","LS010","LS015","LS021","LS044","LS046"],"unresolved_risks":["Primary evidence for the election-delay controversy is explicitly incomplete.","Criminal Code implementation and executive influence need event-level documentation.","The positive institutional context is not balanced by enough precise contrary or corrective evidence."]},"chapter_id":"4B","defensible_evidence_estimate":7,"independent_source_family_estimate":5,"missing_themes":["Primary evidence on election-delay controversy","Executive influence over election institutions","Criminal Code implementation and enforcement","Independent evidence of institutional correction or remedy"],"substantive_issues":["Comparative indices and NGO reports need precise locators and event-level attribution.","Further bounded research is likely to improve the dossier."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"RC014-RC019 separate macroeconomic outcomes, World Bank assessments, project approvals, and formal appointments; page- or box-level locators and distinct claims are needed to avoid inflated counts.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Recovery, appointments, and policy activity were documented alongside inflation, tax, infrastructure, distribution, and social-protection weaknesses; ruler-specific implementation and distribution searches remain incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Missing procurement and audit records, project-level completion and distribution data, subnational reporting, beneficiary evidence, and independent evaluation of appointments.","official_claim_independence":"RC019 supports appointment authority; RC016 supports a project record, but neither independently proves outcomes. World Bank analysis is an external technical check, though much of it relies on official data.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Not directly assessed; beneficiary and service complaints may be more visible in open areas and less visible in marginalized or poorly monitored regions, so volume cannot measure severity.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"World Bank and local indicators address outcomes, inequality, baseline governance, and exposure; learning loss is an outcome, not by itself a personal finding.","closed_system_silence":"Regional inequality, incomplete coverage, and weak monitoring may hide service failures and exclusion, especially where access or reporting is limited.","duplicate_reporting":"World Bank project, human-capital, and COVID materials support multiple distinct claims but require precise locators; local indicators should not be counted as independent narrative sources without source-family review.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Policy activity and long-term gains were considered alongside learning loss, uneven quality, incomplete coverage, and inequality; affordability, quality, regional distribution, and political conditionality remain insufficiently searched.","missing_source_type":"Missing household/beneficiary surveys, school and health administrative records, independent program evaluations, local-language reporting, and regional affordability/distribution data.","official_claim_independence":"World Bank project and analytical records provide external checks but may rely on government data; project approval establishes action and intended design, not realized impact.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Service complaints may exaggerate visible severity in open systems while underserved regions and vulnerable groups may be underreported; no complaint denominator or coverage audit is provided.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"HDI and health/education indicators address population outcomes and baseline; donor, subnational, inherited, and COVID-shock contributions remain material and authority over delivery is shared.","supporting_evidence_ids":["RC016","RC017","RC018","LF1325","LF1333","LF1023","LF1025","LS039","LS047","LS048"],"unresolved_risks":["Target-year affordability, quality, and regional distribution evidence is thin.","Donor and subnational contributions complicate attribution.","Project approval and policy alignment are not outcome evidence."]},"chapter_id":"6B","defensible_evidence_estimate":6,"independent_source_family_estimate":3,"missing_themes":["Affordability and coverage by population","Service quality and regional distribution","Independent evaluation of human-capital programs","Political conditionality or exclusion","Post-shock recovery response within the target period"],"substantive_issues":["National human-development indicators are insufficient to establish ruler-specific delivery quality.","Continuation could materially improve population-level and implementation evidence."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"RC010-RC013 document institutional weakening, reported pressure, formal legal developments, and assessments; they do not establish Widodo's personal enrichment, benefit, deliberate deception, or direct obstruction.","closed_system_silence":"Corruption, favoritism, conflicts, and obstruction are especially vulnerable to concealment; weakened oversight and pressure on monitors increase this risk.","duplicate_reporting":"KPK, civil-society, and legal-reporting claims may overlap; the notebook has few locators and must not count repeated descriptions as independent facts.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse institutional-integrity evidence was searched, but favorable evidence about personal conduct, disclosure, conflicts, enforcement, and corrective action is not comparably developed; direct personal-nexus searches remain incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Missing asset declarations, procurement and beneficial-ownership records, conflict-of-interest disclosures, court findings, audit reports, investigative local journalism, and direct evidence of presidential knowledge or intervention.","official_claim_independence":"RC019 establishes appointment authority, but official institutional records do not independently establish integrity. NGO reporting provides external scrutiny without resolving the personal nexus.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Complaints against monitors may inflate apparent institutional hostility if repeated reporting reflects one campaign; conversely, intimidation and weakened oversight can suppress corruption complaints, so volume is unreliable.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Country corruption indicators establish baseline and institutional exposure, not personal conduct; country corruption indicators and institutional decline are insufficient.","A bounded search for primary integrity and investigative sources could materially improve attribution."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"RC005-RC006 and RC014-RC020 separate formal actions, program records, technical assessments, outcomes, and efficacy limitations; distinct locators and claim units are required, especially for the same program or diplomatic action.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"The notebook includes attributable programs, implementation weaknesses, external-shock dependence, and mixed diplomatic effectiveness; neither complaint volume nor official silence is a reliable effectiveness measure.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"World Bank and local facts address national outcomes and governance baseline; attribution is shared with donors, subnational bodies, prior administrations, and external shocks including COVID recovery and the Ukraine war.","supporting_evidence_ids":["RC005","RC006","RC014","RC015","RC016","RC017","RC018","RC019","RC020","LF1410","LF1447","LS036","LS067","LS076"],"unresolved_risks":["Program ownership is clearer than durable, equitable, independently measured success.","Adaptation and correction evidence is missing.","Diplomatic activity lacks sufficiently independent efficacy assessment.","External shocks and inherited baselines complicate causal interpretation."]},"chapter_id":"8B","defensible_evidence_estimate":8,"independent_source_family_estimate":5,"missing_themes":["Independent implementation and outcome evaluation","Adaptation and corrective action","Durable multi-program results","Distributional and beneficiary evidence","Independent assessment of diplomatic effectiveness"],"substantive_issues":["Formal action and project approval should not be presented as proven effectiveness.","Further bounded research could materially improve implementation, correction, and contrary-evidence coverage."]}],"global_findings":["All eight selected chapters have material research-recoverable gaps; the notebook reports only approximately three unique locators and three approximate source families against substantially higher review thresholds.","The notebook provides useful stable IDs and explicit local-fact dispositions, but the required local-data audit is not explicit and precise locator coverage is inadequate for many mapped claims.","Missing evidence is treated as unresolved rather than negative evidence. National indicators, official statements, gateway material, and contested reports require proportional attribution and independence controls.","No scores, score ranges, anchors, rankings, or judge-directed recommendations were used in this review."],"needs_continuation":true,"reviewer_summary":"Every selected chapter requires bounded continuation because the handoff identifies concrete recoverable gaps in precise locators, source breadth, attribution, contrary evidence, event coverage, or outcome verification. The most acute risk is Chapter 7B's unresolved personal-integrity nexus, followed by 1B's lack of ruler-attributed nuclear-risk evidence and 2B-6B/8B's incomplete primary, local, subnational, implementation, and remedy evidence. Chapters should remain unresolved for confidence and interpretation until those gaps are addressed; no missing evidence is treated as adverse ruler evidence.","schema_version":"ruler_evidence_review_v1","selected_theme_ids":["1B.1","1B.10","1B.2","1B.3","1B.4","1B.5","1B.6","1B.7、1B.8、1B.9"]}
